title: Shipyard Welder
premise: A long master-apprentice drama in the dry-dock welding shed and on the outfitting pier. Xingzi and Alan are easily mistaken for each other; the TIG welding torch goes intact→nozzle-burned→nozzle-replaced; Rust Harbor must be avoided after it capsizes; count memory, false friends, and temporal flashbacks run throughout. Human-readable context only; never fed to the SUT.

states.on_duty_prime: Zhou Lin, a shipyard welder in his thirties, buzz cut, weld scar on the cheekbone, scorched-brown fire suit and steel-toe boots, dark-green TIG welding helmet on the shoulder, rough hands dusted with iron filings.
states.exhausted_injured: The same Zhou Lin: fire-suit cuff burned through, gauze on the left brow, walking slowly with a torch case as cane, gaze heavy but still locked on the weld.
states.deceased: Zhou Lin lies still with eyes closed on an iron bed in the shipyard clinic, face peaceful, breath gone.

states.young_apprentice: Young Xingzi: a lean welding apprentice around fifteen, copper-button work badge on the chest, oversized canvas coveralls, eyes clear and stubborn.
states.adult_successor: Adult Xingzi: a welder in his twenties with broader shoulders, still wearing that copper-button work badge, fitted canvas coveralls, eyes steady.

states.intact: A deep-blue-handled TIG welding torch, tungsten tip bright, gas hose coiled, nozzle undamaged.
states.nozzle_burned: The same TIG welding torch with ceramic nozzle cracked and blackened, tungsten askew, gas hose greasy.
states.nozzle_replaced: The TIG welding torch fitted with a new milky-white ceramic nozzle, tungsten re-sharpened, gas hose wiped clean, ready to restrike an arc.

states.intact: A blue hard-cover weld inspection log with thickness-gauge readouts clipped in, neat writing, clean cover.
states.oil_soaked: The same weld inspection log soaked through with hydraulic oil, cover sticky and curling, writing blurred into a blot.

states.intact: A rust-red riveted barge named Rust Harbor, white-painted name on the gunwale, deck piled with angle steel and a gas-cylinder cage.
states.capsized_sunk: Rust Harbor tips after a crane cable snaps, hull bottom-up half-sunk in dry-dock mud water, mast light out.

states.young_rival: Young welder Alan whose face closely resembles Xingzi's, but wearing charcoal-black long welding gloves and a bright-red epaulette vest over coveralls, manner bold.
states.remade_look: Alan after remaking his look still wears charcoal-black long welding gloves; the epaulette vest is now matte black, manner deeper.

segments.action: At dusk Zhou Lin carries a dark-green welding helmet into the dry-dock welding shed and strikes a test arc with the TIG welding torch.
A row of five brass-hood explosion-proof work lamps hangs on the shed crossbeam; Zhou Lin wipes each glass chimney clean.
Two shift-change bronze bells hang under the shed eaves; Zhou Lin taps them lightly and the dull notes echo.
Zhou Lin checks the TIG welding torch tungsten and gas-hose fitting, confirming no leak.
Through the shed opening Zhou Lin watches rust-red hull outlines in the basin.
The intact TIG welding torch rests on the welding bench, nozzle reflecting the explosion-proof lamps' warm light.
Zhou Lin sits by the slag bin and unscrews his canteen for a few sips.
A distant crane whistle sounds; Zhou Lin puts the helmet back on.
He lightly grinds the bevel to be welded with an angle grinder; sparks briefly fly.
Zhou Lin opens the blue weld inspection log and notes the day's weld numbers in ballpoint.
He sketches the bevel angle in the inspection log and marks thickness readings.
Zhou Lin closes the weld inspection log and tucks it back into the second drawer of the tool cabinet.
Blue-white arc light from the TIG welding torch sweeps across his cheek.
He tears off a scrap of sandpaper and wipes iron powder from his gloves.
At the outfitting pier in the morning Zhou Lin greets the moored rust-red barge Rust Harbor.
Young Xingzi jumps from Rust Harbor onto the pier and loops the cable onto a concrete bollard.
Zhou Lin points to the three enamel electrode-spec tags on the gas-cylinder cage and teaches Xingzi to tell J422 from J506.
Xingzi squats at the pier edge and curiously touches the rivets on Rust Harbor's gunwale.
Zhou Lin explains to Xingzi that when the shipyard shift bells sound twice the arc must stop.
Xingzi looks back at intact Rust Harbor; the copper-button work badge sways lightly on his chest.
Tide slaps the shore; the two walk along the pier toward the dry-dock welding shed.
In the plate-yard narrow aisle Alan in charcoal-black long welding gloves looks back from the upright-plate shadows.

segments.action: In spring flood season Zhou Lin day after day restrikes arcs and patch-welds in the shed.
On another rain night he wraps the fire suit tight and keeps watch by the TIG welding torch.
At high summer noon the shed iron sheet burns hot; he rotates cooling.
In autumn fog the explosion-proof lamps' light struggles through smoke and dust.
On New Year's Eve Zhou Lin alone fills the weld inspection record to the last page.
In early spring he recalibrates the thickness gauge and resumes shipyard patrols.
Before typhoon season Zhou Lin reinforces the gas-cylinder cage straps.
After Frost's Descent he adds a small bucket of dry sand in the shed corner for backup.
In another ship-survey season he taps section by section listening to weld echoes.
On a snow-night shutdown Zhou Lin leaves only one explosion-proof lamp and keeps watch until dawn.
Zhou Lin changes the grinding disc and dresses a newly arrived rib-plate bevel.
He checks the fume-hood filter and shakes out settled weld ash.
He lifts the intact TIG welding torch again and short-arc test-welds a bead.
Rivet-gun rhythm rises from the pier; he looks up to listen.
Zhou Lin drops spent electrode stubs into an iron bucket and closes the lid.
At noon break he smokes outside the shed, tapping ash into a tin can.
In the afternoon he returns to the welding bench and continues patch-welding the manhole coaming.
At sunset he shuts the gas valve and locks the tool cabinet.
At dawn Zhou Lin patrols the outfitting pier; Rust Harbor still lies in the shallow bay.
He crouches to check whether Rust Harbor's gunwale rivets have loosened.
On the gas-cylinder cage those three electrode-spec tags still hang in place.
A blue-gray tug Tide Sound crosses the basin—broad flat hull, not Rust Harbor.
Zhou Lin stands on the pier recording fender wear exposed after the ebb.
He recoils the cable and presses it beside Rust Harbor's deck edge.
A distant crane slowly swings; morning fog begins to thin.
At nightfall Zhou Lin returns to the dry-dock welding shed and opens the oil-soaked weld inspection log.

segments.action: In a rainstorm a crane cable suddenly snaps; the dry-dock welding shed shudders hard.
Standing water floods the welding bench; explosion-proof lamps swing violently.
While Zhou Lin rushes to save gear the TIG welding torch ceramic nozzle cracks black and the tungsten skews.

segments.action: An orange-red mobile welding cart rolls onto the outfitting pier—nothing like the already capsized Rust Harbor.
A yellow-vest white-hat shipyard safety officer jumps onto the pier and talks beside Zhou Lin; the two look similar in build.
The safety officer points at the orange-red mobile welding cart and explains the temporary support grouping.
The welding cart horns and drives off; Zhou Lin alone watches from the pier.
He resets the safety cones and walks back to the shed along the bollards.
Into the plate-yard narrow aisle comes intern Xiaoman in a light-gray headscarf—at a glance somewhat like young Xingzi.
Xiaoman tries tying a cable; Zhou Lin shakes his head—she is not Xingzi after all.
Xiaoman bows and withdraws; only upright-plate shadows remain in the aisle.
At dusk years later Zhou Lin, cuff burned through and brow gauze on, leans on a torch case under the abandoned slipway.
